ex1.mechanism: Polynomial score in bin capacity over item powers, sign-flipped for bins larger than item, then first-differenced along bin order.
ex1.key_move: Root attempt: FunSearch Weibull polynomial with neighbour-difference step.
ex1.why: Proposal only; no excess measured on OR3 or Weibull.

ex2.mechanism: Running histogram of seen item sizes; priority = -residual + 20 × probability a future item closes that residual gap.
ex2.key_move: Root attempt: fill-probability term added to best-fit.
ex2.why: Proposal only; uses only past items so stays online; not measured.

ex3.mechanism: Non-monotone step lookup on residual r = bin - item: tight gaps highest, mid gaps 8-9 lowest, large gaps between.
ex3.key_move: Root attempt: FunSearch OR3 non-monotone step table.
ex3.why: Proposal only; no measured excess on either set.

ex4.mechanism: CMA-ES fits 8 weights of a linear score over residual, item, fill-probability, age, fragment features; trained OR3 half, tested elsewhere.
ex4.key_move: Root attempt: evolution strategy tunes hand-crafted feature weights on OR3 0-9.
ex4.why: Proposal only; OR3-only training risks failing G-WB, unmeasured.

pa1.mechanism: Priority = negative squared residual capacity after placement; argmax equals best fit.
pa1.key_move: Quadratic penalty on leftover gap instead of linear.
pa1.why: Monotone transform of residual yields identical argmax to plain best fit; no measurement.

pa2.mechanism: Harmonic-k with k=6: classify items by interval (C/(i+1), C/i], pack each class in reserved bins with best fit.
pa2.key_move: Segregate items into six harmonic size classes.
pa2.why: Proposal only; class segregation typically wastes space versus best fit; unmeasured.

pa3.mechanism: Replace histogram in fill-probability score with Gaussian kernel density estimate (bandwidth 2) of seen item sizes.
pa3.why: Proposal only; variant of fill-probability scoring, not measured.

pa4.mechanism: Ablate the first-difference step from the Weibull polynomial heuristic and compare excess.

pa5.mechanism: Sample target bin from softmax over best-fit priorities exp(-r/T), T=0.5, instead of argmax.
pa5.key_move: Stochastic softmax selection replaces deterministic argmax.
pa5.why: Proposal only; randomisation likely adds excess over best fit; unmeasured.

pa6.mechanism: CMA-ES tunes 8-feature linear score minimising max over datasets of excess divided by gate threshold.
pa6.key_move: Joint OR3+Weibull minimax objective instead of OR3-only training.
pa6.why: Proposal only; addresses cross-dataset generalisation, unmeasured.

pa7.mechanism: Bounded-space packing: only the 20 most recently opened bins remain eligible; older bins treated closed.
pa7.why: Proposal only; restricting bins can only lose packing opportunities; unmeasured.

pa8.mechanism: Subtract 100 from priority when resulting residual is positive but below smallest item size seen so far.

rn1.mechanism: Priority = negative squared residual capacity after placement; argmax equals best fit.
rn1.why: Same as pa1: monotone transform reduces to best fit; unmeasured.

rn2.mechanism: Six harmonic size classes with reciprocal-integer edges, dedicated bins per class, best fit within class.

rn3.mechanism: Online empirical item-size distribution; favour bin whose residual is most likely closed by a future item, traded with tightness.

rn4.mechanism: Quadratic and cubic capacity/item ratio terms, sign-flipped for roomy bins, then first-differenced along bin order.

rn5.mechanism: Non-monotone residual lookup: tight residuals highest, 8-9 unit residuals lowest, wide residuals intermediate.

rn6.mechanism: CMA-ES fits weights of 8-descriptor linear scorer, trained on half the OR3 set, validated on other half.

rn7.mechanism: Buffer five arriving items and insert them in decreasing size order.
rn7.key_move: Look ahead and reorder items within a window.
rn7.killed_by: G-ONLINE: looks at future items and reorders

rn8.mechanism: Detect benchmark from bin capacity and switch to a dataset-specific scoring rule.
rn8.key_move: Branch heuristic on detected dataset identity.
rn8.why: Capacity-based dataset dispatch is explicitly forbidden.

rn9.mechanism: Subtract a flat constant from the priority of every empty bin so a new bin opens only when no used bin fits.
rn9.key_move: Root idea: flat deduction on unused bins.

rn10.mechanism: Bar small items from bins with at least half capacity free unless no other bin fits, reserving room for large items.
rn10.key_move: Root idea: reserve half-empty bins for large items.

eq1.mechanism: Priority = -r*(1+(r/20)^1.5) on residual r, penalising medium gaps super-linearly while keeping tight fits cheap.
eq1.key_move: Root idea: super-linear closed-form residual penalty.

eq2.mechanism: Prefer exact fit, then smallest remaining gap, opening an empty bin only when no used bin fits: plain best fit.
eq2.key_move: Root idea: exact-fit-first best fit baseline.
eq2.why: Proposal only; equivalent to the best-fit baseline.

vs1.mechanism: Keep a KDE of item sizes on a fixed integer grid updated incrementally per item; bin fill probability becomes a table lookup.
vs1.key_move: Replace #27's per-bin pass over past items with an incremental grid lookup to fix runtime.
vs1.why: Proposal targets #27's 212 s G-TIME failure; unmeasured.

vs2.mechanism: Distil a trained MLP priority into a 32-entry lookup table over residual and item buckets for constant-time scoring.
vs2.key_move: Replace #47's MLP evaluation with a distilled bucket table to cut runtime.
vs2.why: Proposal targets #47's 94 s G-TIME failure; unmeasured.

vs3.mechanism: OR3 step-table priority with break points scaled by the running median item size, adapting to the size distribution online.
vs3.key_move: Express step-table break points in running-median units instead of absolute units.
vs3.why: Proposal targets step tables' Weibull regression; unmeasured.

vs4.mechanism: Weibull polynomial priority plus a penalty when post-placement residual is below the smallest item seen so far.
vs4.key_move: Add unusable-fragment penalty to #16's polynomial to fix its OR3 loss.
vs4.why: Proposal targets #16's OR3 loss from small gaps; unmeasured.

vs5.mechanism: Compute two-item fill probability by FFT convolution of the observed size histogram, refreshed every 500 items.
vs5.key_move: Use FFT and periodic refresh instead of per-item recomputation to cut #65's runtime.
vs5.why: Proposal targets #65's 71 s G-TIME failure; unmeasured.

vs6.mechanism: CMA-ES-trained linear bin scorer with the OR3 step-table score added as a tenth feature for non-monotone gap preference.
vs6.key_move: Add #11 step-table score as a feature to #66's linear model.

vs7.mechanism: Fragment penalty plus OR3 step table for small items, switching to the Weibull polynomial for large items.
vs7.key_move: Route large items to #16's polynomial instead of #36's step table.
vs7.why: Proposal targets #36's Weibull loss on large items; unmeasured.

vs8.mechanism: Closed-gap-fraction table per residual bucket with Bayesian shrinkage of each bucket toward the global closure rate.
vs8.key_move: Add Bayesian shrinkage to #74's bucket estimates to reduce sparse-bucket noise.
vs8.why: Proposal targets #74's G-WB miss from noisy buckets; unmeasured.

vn1.mechanism: KDE fill-probability priority using an Epanechnikov kernel of bandwidth 3 instead of Gaussian.
vn1.key_move: Swap #27's Gaussian kernel for Epanechnikov, bandwidth 3.
vn1.why: Parameter variant; does not address #27's runtime failure; unmeasured.

vn2.mechanism: Weibull polynomial priority with first term (bins - mean(bins))^2 / item instead of using max residual.
vn2.key_move: Replace max with mean bin residual in #16's first term.

vn3.mechanism: Harmonic-k size-class packing with 8 item classes instead of 6.

vn4.mechanism: MLP bin priority with three hidden layers of 8 units, trained by CMA-ES rather than OpenAI-ES.
vn4.key_move: Deeper network and CMA-ES optimiser instead of OpenAI-ES.
vn4.why: Variant does not address #47's runtime failure; unmeasured.

vn5.mechanism: OR3 residual step table with an extra step scoring residual r <= 1 as 5.
vn5.key_move: Add one near-exact-fit step to the table.
vn5.why: Minor variant; does not address the table's Weibull regression; unmeasured.

vn6.mechanism: Sample bins by softmax of priority with temperature annealed from 2 to 0.1 over the stream.
vn6.key_move: Decay softmax temperature over the item stream.

bf1.mechanism: Two-sided fill probability from an online size histogram, with Laplace add-one initialisation to avoid division by zero.
bf1.key_move: Fix #28's first-item ZeroDivisionError with Laplace counts; mechanism unchanged.
bf1.why: Bug-fix retry so #28's mechanism can be measured; unmeasured.

bf2.mechanism: Percentile fragment penalty masking residuals below the 10th-percentile item size, with residual sign corrected to bins - item.
bf2.key_move: Fix #34's sign-flipped residual so the mask actually fires.
bf2.why: #34 never exercised its mechanism; retry measures it as designed.

bf3.mechanism: Replace singular features 1/r and item/r with 1/(r+0.5) and item/(r+0.5) so CMA-ES-tuned linear priority stays finite at exact fits.
bf3.key_move: Regularise the divergent 1/r features by adding 0.5 to r, then rerun #45.
bf3.why: Proposal only; fixes #45's infinite-feature collapse at r=0, no measurement recorded yet.

bf4.mechanism: Reset the adaptive module-level count table only at instance start, detected by all bins at full capacity, not on every priority call.
bf4.key_move: Move the table reset from function entry to fresh-instance detection, then measure #75.
bf4.why: Proposal only; repairs a bug that erased #75's adaptive statistics every call; no result yet.

bu1.mechanism: Reimplement #28's two-sided fill-probability priority unchanged, assuming the earlier crash was an implementation slip.
bu1.key_move: Plain rerun of #28 with no diagnosed cause or change.
bu1.why: No diagnosis of #28's failure; a repeat without a named fix adds nothing new.

bu2.mechanism: Rerun #45's CMA-ES feature priority with cleaner code, attributing the collapse to a numerical glitch.
bu2.key_move: Plain rerun of #45 without fixing the infinite 1/r features.
bu2.why: Ignores known cause (1/r infinite at r=0); bf3 names the actual fix.

bff1.mechanism: Correct Harmonic-4 class assignment to floor(C/item)-1 so boundary-size items fall in the right class, then measure.
bff1.key_move: Fix off-by-one class boundary so size-75 items land in class 2.
bff1.why: Proposal only; bug fix enabling a fair Harmonic-4 measurement, not yet run.

lk1.mechanism: Track each bin's last-fill step and add to -r a bonus for longest-untouched bins so stale bins close first.
lk1.key_move: Add bin age (time since last item) bonus to best-fit score.
lk1.why: Proposal only; tests whether bin staleness helps close gaps; no measurement.

lk2.mechanism: Sum-of-Squares: pick bin minimising sum over gap sizes of squared counts of open bins with that residual after placement.
lk2.key_move: Square counts of each gap size across bins rather than residuals.
lk2.why: Proposal only; classic Csirik SS algorithm, not yet measured on OR3/Weibull.

lk3.mechanism: For each candidate bin, sample 30 future items from running size histogram, best-fit them, choose bin with fewest new bins opened.
lk3.object: Monte Carlo rollouts from size histogram
lk3.key_move: Simulate future from observed histogram instead of scoring gap closure analytically.
lk3.killed_by: G-TIME risk: rollouts per candidate on 5,000-item instances
lk3.why: Proposal only; lookahead by simulation of past-distribution items; cost may threaten 60 s limit.

lk4.mechanism: Every 1,000 items solve LP relaxation on prefix size histogram; score bins by dual values of sizes that can fill residual.
lk4.object: LP dual prices on prefix histogram
lk4.key_move: Replace L1-bound guidance with LP-relaxation dual prices from the prefix.
lk4.why: Proposal only; dual-price guided placement, not yet measured.

lk5.mechanism: Evaluate #11's step table with np.searchsorted over break points, removing per-bin Python loop while keeping scores identical.
lk5.key_move: Vectorise table lookup; scores unchanged, only runtime reduced.
lk5.why: Speed-only change; cannot alter excess, only G-TIME behaviour.

lk6.mechanism: Use worst fit for the first 5% of the stream to diversify gap sizes, then switch to best fit.
lk6.key_move: Worst-fit warm-up phase before best fit.
lk6.why: Proposal only; tests whether early gap diversity helps later packing.

lk7.mechanism: Use item minus previous item to predict a large next item and avoid filling residuals such an item would need.
lk7.key_move: Predict next item size from recent stream trend to reserve gaps.
lk7.why: Proposal only; assumes serial correlation in sizes, likely absent in i.i.d. benchmark streams.

lk8.mechanism: Penalise bins by variance of item sizes already inside, favouring homogeneous bins, with -r tie-break.
lk8.key_move: Add content-homogeneity penalty to best-fit score.

lk9.mechanism: Place item in the bin the previous item went to when it fits, else best fit, exploiting runs of similar sizes.
lk9.key_move: Stickiness to previous item's bin before falling back to best fit.
lk9.why: Proposal only; relies on size runs, likely absent in i.i.d. streams.

lk10.mechanism: priority = -r - kappa * item count in bin, completing bins with few large items before bins of many small items.
lk10.key_move: Add item-count penalty to best-fit score.

nv1.mechanism: Predict size frequencies from prefix, build offline profile of bin types, route arrivals into profile slots, opening new copies when full.
nv1.key_move: Learning-augmented profile packing from predicted frequencies.
nv1.why: Proposal only; profile packing from prefix-learned distribution, not yet measured.

nv2.mechanism: Bucket open bins into 10 gap classes; choose placement minimising value function on class-count vector fitted by value iteration on simulations.
nv2.key_move: Approximate DP with fitted value function over gap-class counts.
nv2.why: Proposal only; RL/ADP placement policy, unmeasured.

nv3.mechanism: UCB1 bandit per size bucket selects best fit, OR3 table or Weibull polynomial per arrival, rewarded by waste change vs running bound.
nv3.key_move: Online bandit mixing of existing dataset-specialised heuristics.
nv3.killed_by: G-ONLINE risk if selection acts as dataset-identity branching
nv3.why: Proposal only; adaptive portfolio selection among prior heuristics, unmeasured.

nv4.mechanism: Genetic programming over expression trees of r, item, bin age and gap-count features, bred on both datasets and symbolically simplified.
nv4.key_move: GP search over expression trees with joint two-dataset fitness.
nv4.why: Proposal only; generic evolved-formula search, unmeasured.

pd1.mechanism: Every 1,000 items run FFD on prefix, use resulting bin types and proportions as template, steer placements to complete template bins, else best fit.
pd1.key_move: Profile template from offline FFD on prefix instead of predicted frequencies.
pd1.why: Proposal only; prefix profile packing variant, unmeasured.

pd2.mechanism: Periodically re-run offline first-fit-decreasing on the items seen so far, extract frequent bin compositions, and route each arriving item into an open slot of the most-needed composition.
pd2.key_move: Root attempt: online routing toward compositions mined from offline FFD packing of the prefix.
pd2.why: Proposal only, with no run or excess numbers. It needs the item history, which priority(item, bins) may not expose, and its time cost is unmeasured.

pd3.mechanism: After each tentative insertion, count bins that share each leftover capacity, sum the squared counts, and pick the insertion that minimises this total.
pd3.key_move: Root attempt: scores each placement by how concentrated the residual-capacity histogram becomes (sum of squared counts).
pd3.why: Proposal only; no OR3 or Weibull excess was measured.

pd4.mechanism: For each feasible bin, simulate a few dozen future arrivals sampled from the empirical size distribution with best-fit, and choose the bin whose simulations open the fewest new bins.
pd4.object: Monte Carlo rollout per candidate bin
pd4.key_move: Root attempt: lookahead by sampled rollouts from the observed size law rather than a static score.
pd4.why: Proposal only. G-TIME risk on 5,000-item instances is unmeasured, and the empirical size law needs history that priority(item, bins) may not have.

pl1.mechanism: Among bins within 1 unit of the tightest fit, break ties by the placement that minimises the sum of squared residuals over all open bins.
pl1.key_move: Root attempt: adds a global sum-of-squared-residuals tie-break inside a near-best-fit window.
pl1.why: Proposal only; no excess was measured on either set.

pl2.mechanism: Compute the L1 lower bound of the prefix to set a target fill per bin, and penalise bins whose post-placement fill exceeds the running average target by more than one item size.
pl2.key_move: Takes the target from the prefix L1 lower bound instead of from an offline packing template.
pl2.why: Proposal only; no excess was measured. Needs only total size so far, which can be computed from bin fills.
